earlier_scan.source_named: Troike, Rudolph C. 1959. A descriptive phonology and morphology of Coahuilteco. UT Austin diss; also Troike 1996 HNAI-17 sketch. Not online; Swanton 1940 (read on archive.org) has no stress statement.

sources.citation: García, Bartholomé. 1760. Manual para administrar los santos sacramentos de penitencia, eucharistia, extrema-uncion, y matrimonio.. Mexico: Imprenta de los herederos de Doña Maria de Rivera. 8 prelim. leaves + 88 pp. Newberry Library scan (Ayer 871.C50 C36 G2 1760).
sources.note: The sole primary source. 'Advertencias Prologales' (leaf A recto, p. 21; verified on the page scan) explain the diacritics: the accent marks on vowels (â ê î ô û and á é í ó ú) mean the vowel 'se pronunciarán largos' (are pronounced long); the apostrophe marks fortis/ejective consonants. Nothing whatever on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Coahuilteco language' (en) and 'Idioma coahuilteco' (es), phonology sections citing Troike 1996.
sources.note: Only 'Coahuilteco has both short and long vowels' / 'El coahuilteco tiene tanto vocales cortas como largas'; no stress information.

sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1940. Linguistic material from the tribes of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 127. Washington: GPO.
sources.note: 'Phonetics', p. 8: García's two accent series 'merely indicated long vowels'; Swanton substitutes a length sign for the acute and circumflex accents. No statement about stress anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full scanned: 'stress' and 'accent' hit only the orthographic remarks and Gatschet's Comecrudo/Cotoname/Karankawa accents).

sources.citation: Sapir, Edward. 1920. The Hokan and Coahuiltecan languages. International Journal of American Linguistics 1(4): 280-290.
sources.note: Comparative lexical/phonetic correspondences; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Pimentel, Francisco. 1874. Cuadro descriptivo y comparativo de las lenguas indígenas de México, 2nd ed., vol. 2, cap. XIX 'El Tejano ó Coahuilteco', pp. 73-79 (and cap. XX comparisons, pp. 81ff.). Mexico: Isidoro Epstein.
sources.note: §3 'Pronunciación' reprints García's Advertencias verbatim (accents = long vowels); §4 'Sílabas' says only that the language is polysyllabic. No stress statement.
Lists sources Troike 1959 and Troike 1996; no stress data.

sources.citation: García, (George) Michael. 2022/2023. Gramática de la Lengua Coahuilteca (2022, 39 pp., academia.edu document 80641972) / Grammar of the Coahuilteco Language (English version, 2023, 39 pp., academia.edu document 98707641). Self-published compilation, academia.edu.

tone.summary: Says nothing about tone; a compiled grammar sketch whose pronunciation section gives five vowels with contrastive length, a consonant chart with ejectives, and the colonial vs modern spelling.

sources.citation: Acosta, Miguel Rodarte. 2022. Coahuilteco Language Reclamation Program. MA thesis, The University of Arizona. 76 pp. (ProQuest Dissertations & Theses 30243535; UA Campus Repository hdl 10150/667945).

tone.summary: No tone or stress described; Garcia's acute/circumflex accents = vowel length (5 short + 5 long vowels); glottalized consonant series.
